title: Newmarket shooting draws inquest
article: An inquest is scheduled to begin Monday in the death of a man shot dead by York Regional Police in Newmarket about three years ago.Evan Arnold was pronounced dead at Southlake Regional Health Centre following a September 2006 home invasion.The provincial Special Investigations Unit concluded the shooting was legally justified.The inquest will examine the circumstances surrounding Mr. Arnold's death and the jury can make recommendations aimed at preventing similar deaths, according to the coroner. Under the Coroner's Act, an inquest is mandatory when a person dies while in custody.The inquest, to be held at Aurora Town Hall, is expected to last one week and will hear from about 10 witnesses.Both York police and the coroners' office declined comment this week.York police received a call from a woman who said a man had broken into her Southwind Court home, the SIU said. The man told the woman the police were after him and ordered her out of her home.Officers responded, pulled out their guns and surrounded the house. One officer ran up the driveway and tried to open the front door but it was locked. He was about to walk away when the man, holding two large knives, opened the door.Police yelled at him to drop the knives but he shouted "You will have to kill me" and slammed the door closed, the SIU said.The officers knew back-up was on the way and were about to move away from the home when the door opened again. The man was still holding the knives and appeared agitated, the SIU said."He told the officers that he had just tried to cut himself inside the home and had nothing to live for," the SIU said. "He also said that if one of the officers did not kill him, he was going to kill an officer."After that, one officer holstered his gun and told him the police were backing off. Four officers still had their guns drawn and repeatedly told the man to drop the knives or go back inside. Instead, he ran and raised the knives to an officer. The officer fired two shots at the man, who was between three and 10 feet away. He was hit twice and fatally wounded.
